newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS-Manila shares seen plagued by property, U.S. market.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Manila shares seen plagued by property, U.S. market.

text.p: Philippine shares finished higher on Friday in modest volume but analysts said despite the uptick, apprehension on the property sector continued to plague the market.
The main index rose by 17.11 points to 2,944.48 but week-on-week, the stock market's barometer fell by 31.8 points, or 1.07 percent, from 2,976.78 points the previous Friday.

Most blue chips San Miguel Corp B, Metropolitan Bank & Trust Co and First Philippine Holdings Corp trudged higher, propping up the main index but in the broader market, losers swamped gainers 74 to 44.
Concerns of a surplus in the property sector hammered stocks Empire East Land Holdings Inc and Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc on Friday.
Empire East closed at its lowest ever at 5.20 pesos, less than half of its initial public offering (IPO) price of 12.90 pesos last year. Megaworld, on the other hand, hit a year low of 5.20 pesos.
Analysts said the market next week will continue to suffer the brunt of the troubled property sector exacerbated by concerns on rising U.S. interest rates.

"The bias will continue to be downwards as there will be the same concerns as the past weeks. Everybody is still worried about the property and banking sector, nerves have to be calmed," said Erwin Tan, research director at Abacus Securities Corp.
"The question to be answered is how much the market should really be valued," Tan added.
Leila Calderon, senior investment analyst at Asian Capital Equities, said rebounds may be seen but they would be technical in nature.
"Foreign investors are still looking at the U.S. market, expectations are still high that the Fed will raise rates and we are still hunted by the property sector issue," said Calderon.
Lisa Joson, research head at Amsteel Securities Phils Inc, said the market next week will continue to consolidate with support seen at 2,850 points.
